crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: GDP Nowcasting
children.blurb: GDP nowcasting is the practice of estimating the current quarter's gross domestic product before the official statistic is published.

children.name: Reading Central Bank Communication
children.blurb: Reading central bank communication is the systematic study of what monetary policy makers say and write, from rate decisions and statements to minutes, speeches, interviews and press conferences.

children.name: Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis
children.blurb: Synthetic populations for policy analysis are artificial datasets of people, households, firms, or places that match the statistical properties of a real population.

children.name: Climate and the Economy
children.blurb: Climate and the Economy in macroeconomic econometrics covers how weather shocks, gradual warming, and climate policy affect aggregate outcomes such as output, inflation, employment, investment, and trade.

children.name: Agent-Based and Game Theory Models
children.blurb: Agent-based and game theory models in macroeconomic econometrics study economies as systems of interacting decision makers rather than as a single representative agent.

sections.body: Macroeconomic econometrics is the part of economics that measures and forecasts whole economies, and AI is now doing much of that measurement through pattern finding in large, messy data sets. GDP nowcasting uses machine learning on high frequency indicators such as payments, shipping, electricity use, satellite images and web text to estimate current output before official statistics arrive. Reading central bank communication applies natural language processing to speeches, minutes and statements to score tone, uncertainty and policy direction. Synthetic populations for policy analysis generate artificial households or individuals that preserve statistical properties of real survey data, which lets researchers test tax, benefit or energy policies without exposing personal records. Climate and the economy work uses AI to link emissions, weather, damage and growth over long horizons, often inside integrated assessment models. Agent based and game theory models simulate many decision makers who react to one another, which helps study bubbles, runs, bargaining and policy games.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Where the work stands is mixed. Nowcasting has become a practical tool for tracking activity in real time, but it does not solve the fundamental problem that GDP is revised and that relationships between indicators shift during crises. Reading central bank communication can reliably extract broad sentiment and topic, yet it struggles with conditionality, irony, forward guidance and the difference between what a central bank says and what it will do. Synthetic populations are useful for privacy preserving scenario analysis, but their value depends on how well they match real distributions and on whether they capture behavioural responses rather than just demographic averages. Climate and the economy models face deep uncertainty about damage functions, tipping points, technology change and long run growth, so their outputs are scenarios rather than predictions. Agent based and game theory models can produce rich dynamics and strategic behaviour, but they often have many parameters that are hard to estimate, and they are rarely validated against out of sample macro data. The honest limit across all these areas is that AI is better at measurement and pattern detection than at causal inference, and macro data are short, nonstationary and full of structural breaks.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section fit together as a chain from short run monitoring to long run simulation. GDP Nowcasting is the entry point for tracking current activity with high frequency data and machine learning. Reading Central Bank Communication shows how text from policy institutions becomes a measurable input for expectations and interest rate paths. Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis provides the micro level foundation for testing distributional effects when real micro data are restricted or too small. Climate and the Economy extends the horizon to physical risks, transition policies and global growth, where AI helps combine climate science with economic models. Agent-Based and Game Theory Models supplies the strategic and heterogeneous agent layer that connects individual behaviour to aggregate outcomes. A reader would go to each page for its specific method and evidence, and together they show how AI is changing measurement, interpretation and simulation in macroeconomics.
